USD.catalyst: The US Dollar Index trades near 103.59, consolidating above its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages as markets digest persistent policy divergence and a third consecutive hot core CPI reading. CME FedWatch pricing indicates an approximately 95% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the conclusion of the FOMC meeting on December 9, 2026, alongside reports that Goldman Sachs anticipates two further Federal Reserve rate increases prior to an extended pause. Fed Governor Beth Hammack is scheduled to deliver remarks today at 14:30 GMT, closely following October US Industrial Production, which is expected to print at 0.1% month-over-month. In addition to monetary policy support, geopolitical cross-currents and trade friction remain elevated after Washington introduced new chip export licensing mandates across five jurisdictions to restrict Chinese data center access.

GBP.catalyst: Sterling maintains modest composite weekly gains of +0.08% across the G10, though it remains technically constrained below its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving average cluster between 1.3334 and 1.3410 against the dollar. The currency continues to reflect the aftermath of the Bank of England's recent 25-basis-point rate hike, which passed via an unexpectedly hawkish 9–0 unanimous vote against a forecast 7–2 split, accompanied by MPC projections that inflation will re-accelerate to 4.9% by mid-2027. Despite a 27-basis-point expansion in the UK-US 2-year sovereign yield spread over the past 20 days in the pound's favor, upward momentum has been tempered ahead of labor market figures and the upcoming October UK CPI report scheduled for November 18, which is expected to print unchanged at 3.5% year-over-year.

EUR.catalyst: The euro holds steady on a daily composite basis but remains under broader pressure near 19-month lows against the dollar, trading entirely beneath its descending 20-day moving average at 1.1164 and 200-day average at 1.1523. Macro sentiment remains dampened by second-estimate Eurozone Q3 GDP confirming stagnating momentum alongside ongoing political gridlock in France. Policy guidance from Frankfurt remains actively hawkish, with Deutsche Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel stating that another rate increase is "highly probable" due to energy-driven inflation, while Dutch central bank Governor Klaas Knot cautioned that ECB bond market interventions cannot replace sound fiscal policy. Markets are currently pricing around 60 basis points of cumulative ECB tightening over the next six months, with market participants awaiting formal remarks from ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane later today. CFTC positioning shows institutional leveraged accounts heavily net short the shared currency at -98,604 contracts.

JPY.catalyst: The Japanese yen stands as the strongest weekly performer across the G10 with a +0.90% composite advance across seven pairs, supported by tightening expectations and acute FX intervention vigilance. Although Q3 GDP unexpectedly contracted by 0.1% quarter-on-quarter annualized against consensus expectations for a 0.2% expansion, markets maintain an 85% implied probability of a 25-basis-point Bank of Japan rate hike in December. Hawkish domestic commentary has accelerated, with BOJ Policy Board member Hajime Takata urging a "nimble approach" to further tightening and suggesting Japan's neutral rate may exceed current estimates, while former BOJ Governor Haruhiko Kuroda remarked that policy rates may ultimately need to rise above neutral. In options markets, 1-month 25-delta risk reversals trade at an extreme downside-skewed -1.74 against spot near the 160.00 psychological threshold, with traders focusing on Japan's October trade balance release due at 23:50 GMT.

AUD.catalyst: The Australian dollar remains pressured over the weekly horizon with a -0.76% composite decline across G10 peers, trading well below its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages. The Reserve Bank of Australia released the minutes from its recent 6-3 policy vote today, revealing that six board members judged current cash rates were "not clearly sufficient" to contain inflation risks, while three members expressed caution over a potentially sharper economic downturn. This hawkish tilt was reinforced by RBA Governor Michele Bullock, who emphasized on a panel that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside, pushing back against expectations of a definitive December policy pause. The currency now faces immediate domestic focus on the Australian Wage Price Index scheduled for release on Wednesday.

CAD.catalyst: The Canadian dollar softened on a composite daily basis following domestic data showing October CPI decelerated to 3.1% year-over-year against forecasts of 3.2%. The inflation miss prompted a sharp repricing in short-term interest rates, reducing market-implied odds of a December Bank of Canada rate hike from 54% to 38%. The currency faces additional pressure from a pullback in crude oil prices, keeping it trading below its 20-day moving average against the greenback at 1.4080. External headwinds also persist surrounding upcoming CUSMA negotiations and prospective US tariff risks, even as the Bank of Canada and the People's Bank of China formally enacted a bilateral local currency swap facility.

CHF.catalyst: The Swiss franc displays neutral composite performance across the G10 today, holding essentially flat on both a daily (+0.00%) and 1-week (-0.01%) basis. The franc remains structurally depressed against the US dollar, trading below its 20-day moving average of 0.8256 as broad dollar demand and rising US Treasury yields dominate global FX flows. Domestic drivers have remained muted, with local sentiment supported at the margin by equity performance after an earnings beat by Richemont lifted the Swiss Market Index by 0.57%. In the absence of fresh monetary policy addresses from the Swiss National Bank, the currency is largely range-bound against European peers and dictated by broader risk sentiment and sovereign yield differentials.

NZD.catalyst: The New Zealand dollar has underperformed over the past week, declining -0.58% on a composite G10 basis and hovering near multi-month lows below its 20-day moving average at 0.5621 against the dollar. Pressure intensified following the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's fourth-quarter survey of expectations, where the two-year inflation expectations gauge inched up only marginally to 2.36% from the prior quarter, failing to justify aggressive policy tightening despite one-year expectations jumping to 2.92%. Survey respondents project the Official Cash Rate to reach 3.05% by year-end compared to the current 2.75% benchmark ahead of the RBNZ's upcoming Monetary Policy Statement on December 9. Separately, domestic October food prices fell 0.4% month-over-month, while the RBNZ highlighted rising external risks, citing elevated global bond yields, Middle East tensions, and equity market valuations.

Recent Norges Bank staff analysis noted that cyclical fluctuations in EUR/NOK continue to be heavily dictated by relative inflation and cross-border monetary policy news shocks. In the absence of tier-one domestic economic releases or immediate Norges Bank policy events this week, the krone remains primarily tethered to crude oil benchmark fluctuations and global risk sentiment.

While Scandinavian central banks continue to coordinate regional liquidity access via the Scandinavian Cash Pool alongside Norges Bank and Danmarks Nationalbank, Swedish domestic data catalysts remain scarce this week, leaving the currency sensitive to broader European growth trends and external rate dynamics.
